title: Dispatch OGF 3: Last Branch Bears Scenes of a City in Flight
summary: Several fruit show the same evacuation from different windows and streets.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: A new cluster of glass pears has formed on the orchard’s western graft. Unlike the first harvest, these do not show incidents from years past. Each contains a view of Alderwick residents leaving the northern quarter with handcarts, bedding, and children. The market clock reads 4:12 in two of the scenes.

Miss Agnes Morrow, the municipal archivist, recognized the doorway of her own building. It appears boarded, and water covers the first step. In another pear, Mr. Fenner’s cart crosses the east bridge laden with strangers. He has neither agreed to lend it nor been told to evacuate.

Dr. Saye has compared the scenes with streets and faces visible today. She will not call them a forecast. Some fruit from the earlier harvest showed private acts from vantage points no person occupied. These new images could likewise belong to an unobserved course in the Eidetic Stratum. Their agreement, she says, warrants immediate investigation.

Mrs. Rill has declined requests from officials to pick the remaining fruit. One scene places her orchard at the center of a pale brightness above the houses. “People will blame us before they know what they are looking at,” she said. She has agreed to allow the Institute onto the land with its measuring apparatus.

The council has asked residents not to leave their homes on the strength of an image in a pear. It has also ordered a survey of the Northmere Reservoir, whose lower wall stands above the district shown under water.
